cases.title: Maharashtra afforestation: claimed utilization versus money and surviving trees
cases.question: Can state utilization claims reconcile to dated transfers, paid work and independently measured plantation survival?
cases.summary: A newly tabled national audit and October reporting expose a testable discrepancy in historical Maharashtra scheme reporting. Mumbai denotes state oversight and Pune denotes Bhor district context; sampled works span several districts, not city-centre plantations.

observations.text: The 2026 publication audits 2015–16 to March 2025; it is not a claim that all sampled failures happened in 2026.

The Indian Express reports ₹17.17 crore released to Maharashtra SFDA in 2018–19, ₹12.75 crore claimed utilized, ₹9.26 crore released to five FDAs and ₹0.29 crore found used. These differently scoped stages must be reconciled, not subtracted into an invented theft total.
Reported Rayari (Bhor) survival was 96%, while the audit inspection reported under 5%; missing soil-moisture work and inadequate protection are measurable delivery concerns.

counterevidence.text: Original report records state explanations of missing matching share and overlapping committee membership; delayed funds and cattle damage can explain poor survival without proving diversion.
The state reported opening a new SNA savings account from September 2021. This is a remedial claim to verify; it does not reconcile every earlier certificate.

cases.title: Tara revised coal block: ownership, boundary change and clearance gates
cases.question: Does the revised auction boundary and clearance record resolve the earlier ecological objections before any extraction begins?
cases.summary: September official and opposition statements disagree on the consequences of reopening Tara. An original company filing establishes the CG Syn-Gas → Mundra Synenergy → Adani Enterprises ownership chain as a separate branch; the reported auction-winner name is held unmerged until the exact award identity is verified. Raipur is the state decision hub; the mine is in Hasdeo-Arand.

observations.text: PIB says the block was removed in July 2023, reintroduced after a December 11, 2025 state letter and CMPDIL boundary revision, with nine bids and a 37.50% revenue-share result.

The company’s August 23, 2025 filing documents MSEL as AEL’s wholly owned subsidiary and its incorporation of CSGCL with 100% holding and ₹5 lakh subscribed capital. This is historical capitalization, not project financing.
₹1,200 crore annual revenue and over 8,000 jobs are Ministry projections; this archive does not represent them as received money or verified employment.
The reported winner and incorporated company have closely similar names, but this graph does not merge them. The award/CIN match is a visible missing identity hop.

counterevidence.text: Government says the revised block excludes the Lemru corridor influence zone and no tree felling/mining may begin before statutory approvals. These are concrete claims to test against GIS and clearance orders.
Opposition forest-loss figures and allegations of political favoritism are not independently measured or established by the materials admitted here.
A newly incorporated project subsidiary and small initial capital can be normal project structuring; eligibility and parent-support terms, not incorporation alone, decide financing adequacy.

cases.title: Goa mining FIR quashed: update the legal graph before tracing recoveries
cases.question: Which independently evidenced recovery or prosecution tracks, if any, survive the reported quashing of this specific FIR?
cases.summary: July reports materially change the legal status of a 2013 Shah Commission-based proceeding. The investigation separates this quashed FIR from individual mining cases and any civil/statutory recoveries, rather than keeping every historical allegation active.

observations.text: The Goan identifies seven applicants including Salgaocar Mining Industries Pvt Ltd and reports the FIR quashed after its foundational direction was set aside.
TOI reports the court cited a 2013 Supreme Court stay, lack of investigative progress and the state’s undertaking not to act solely on commission findings.
₹35,000 crore is a historical commission estimate, not a judgment fixing liability against these applicants or a traceable money transfer.

counterevidence.text: Defence argued the case’s foundation had fallen and prolonged prosecution was unjustified; quashing is a substantive update that defeats an unchanged active-FIR claim.
A procedural quashing does not establish every separate extraction or recovery claim was false; each separate case requires its own evidence and outcome.

cases.title: Mithi flood works: test the quantity records against the bail counterevidence
cases.question: Do source-level machinery, weighbridge and site-inspection records establish payment for work not delivered, or defeat that suspicion?
cases.summary: October reporting describes continued desilting inquiries. The April bail court’s reported machinery and certification findings materially weaken a central prosecution premise and stay beside every related hypothesis.

observations.text: EOW alleges ₹65.54 crore loss and manipulation of equipment terms, rental pricing and silt quantities; admitted sources do not include the original bill-by-bill loss calculation.
Reports describe BMC tender specifications matching Matprop equipment and involvement of Virgo Specialties in machine supply. These are investigation claims, not concluded collusion.
October reporting says Dino Morea was questioned, not named as accused, and denied arrest. No Morea-to-minister or proceeds-beneficiary graph edge is asserted here.

counterevidence.text: April 22 bail reasoning reportedly found procurement and allotment documents for two machines and certification by BMC officials. It also found Kadam or his companies did not hold the desilting work contract and third-party machine provision was permitted.
Defence said further custody was unnecessary after charge sheet; the judge recorded no criminal history. Neither public association nor older accusation establishes propensity.
Flooding can result from rainfall, downstream bottlenecks and maintenance deficiencies; a flood event alone cannot prove false billing.

cases.title: Ahmedabad police land: cancelled auction, statutory clearance and public-use value
cases.question: Was the change from commercial auction to police allocation lawfully valued and supported by a documented service need?
cases.summary: September reporting describes Makarba plot96 reallocated for police use after a commercial sale could not be registered. The ₹38.52 crore difference is an opportunity-cost question, not evidence that anyone received that amount.

observations.text: Both reports identify TP84/A final plot96 and a ₹68.44 crore commercial bid versus ₹29.92 crore base value; the later report identifies Tameer Infrastructure as bidder and police as intended recipient.

The earlier account says the deputy collector denied Disturbed Areas Act clearance, preventing the deed. The later account cites September 24 standing-committee approval and MLA Amit Thaker’s security representations.
The reports conflict on the initial auction date; exact chronology remains held pending original municipal minutes.

counterevidence.text: A needed police station is a public-service asset and can justify foregoing a higher commercial bid; the public benefit must be evaluated rather than assumed to be corruption.
Registration was reportedly barred by statutory permission refusal, which is an alternative explanation for cancellation independent of the later police allocation.

nextRecords.purpose: Determine legal basis and whether the commercial transaction could lawfully complete.

cases.title: Shivpuri defence manufacturing: announced capex versus financing and public support
cases.question: Which legal project entity, funding instruments and public support conditions will underwrite the announced investment?
cases.summary: The July 5 company filing announces ₹2,500 crore planned defence manufacturing capex and forecast jobs. This is an ongoing project-monitoring case from just outside the latest window, with no established impropriety and no evidence here of a government purchase award.

observations.text: Company announced groundbreaking July 5, 2026 and planned ₹2,500 crore investment with forecast 5,000 direct/indirect jobs. Neither figure is verified expenditure or delivered employment.
A separate news report describes an approximately three-year operational target; underlying milestone agreement remains unavailable.
The public release names political office holders and company leadership attending or endorsing the project. Attendance is recorded as public context, not as a financial relationship.

counterevidence.text: Indigenous supply-chain development, domestic employment and industrial capability are stated legitimate objectives. A private defence investment announcement is not itself a procurement irregularity.

No admitted source establishes the project’s exact SPV, public subsidy, concessional land price, foreign equity, secured lender or an armed-forces order. These remain acquisition gaps, not hidden-money findings.
